description: This bar chart, from the paper “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media,” illustrates the average number of likes for posts categorized by their similarity to other posts, measured in terms of the number of posts in their most similar group. The horizontal axis, labeled “Most similar group of posts,” displays five discrete, equally spaced categorical bins: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450], representing ranges of post similarity. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, is a linear scale ranging from 400 to 550, with major tick marks at 400, 450, 500, and 550, indicating the average number of likes per post in each group. Each bar is light blue and has an error bar extending vertically from its top, indicating variability in the average like count. The bars are arranged in ascending order of the group’s post count, from left to right. The bar for the (0,90] group is the tallest, reaching approximately 545 likes. The bar for the (90,180] group is the shortest, at approximately 530 likes. The bars for the (180,270] and (270,360] groups are visually similar in height, both around 540 likes. The bar for the (360,450] group is slightly shorter than the (0,90] group, at approximately 540 likes. There is no legend or additional visual emphasis such as shading or bolding for any particular bar.
